visual_argument: Every count in League City's record is laid in the material of a public road, white thermoplastic on Gulf Coast asphalt, because Proposition A defines the cameras by where they stand: fixed locations on public roadways. One stripe, bar, marker or groove is one counted thing, so a reader counts the record without the headline.
build_risk: Frame 5 lays the three roll calls as three crosswalks across one lane, one behind another, through txthree: 7 worn bars farthest, 7 fresh bars beside one bare saw cut, 8 fresh bars nearest. The audition's first reading charged the planned plan relief as a bevelled tile chart, so it was rebuilt as this oblique, the plan's own fallback.
distinct_from_recent: No. 63 was a brass balance and weights on a chalk plinth, warm metal, blued accent. No. 62 was turbine tower sections and survey stakes on caliche, mesquite accent. No. 61 was a delivery drone and a lattice dock tower, dusk gold accent. No. 39, the last Flock deck, carried a plate reader on its pole at blue hour through nine frames. This deck shows no camera at all: its subject is road paint, cut grooves and raised markers on black asphalt, a cold matte white against a terracotta accent at the kerb.
